Title: Replace client-trusted auth with enforced server-side authz
Acceptance Criteria: All protected APIs require authenticated identity; server enforces role checks; UI role spoofing fails; privileged access cannot be obtained from client state alone.

Title: Remove or lock down privilege escalation endpoints
Acceptance Criteria: No unauthenticated role change endpoints exist; admin-only routes require verified admin authz; all role changes are audited with before/after values.

Title: Bind tenant access to identity entitlements
Acceptance Criteria: Tenant context is derived from authenticated scope; arbitrary tenant header switching is rejected; cross-tenant access tests pass.

Title: Secret hygiene and artifact scanning in CI/CD
Acceptance Criteria: No secrets in repo/images/bundles/logs; secret scan and artifact-content validation run in CI; all previously exposed secrets rotated.

Title: Session hardening and revocation
Acceptance Criteria: Short-lived sessions/tokens implemented; refresh flow defined; forced logout supported; expired sessions fail safely and cleanly in UI.

Title: Step-up approval for dangerous actions
Acceptance Criteria: Kill-switch clear, strategy enable, capital-limit changes, and break-glass require stronger auth or maker-checker approval; all such actions are audited.

Title: Centralized immutable audit store
Acceptance Criteria: Audit events are append-only, centralized, queryable, and durable; tampering is detectable; local JSONL is no longer the system of record.

Title: Full decision lineage for every trade
Acceptance Criteria: Each order/trade links to strategy version, model version, inputs, regime, policy results, risk checks, and execution outcome; replay artifact exists.

Title: Configuration and strategy approval workflow
Acceptance Criteria: Production config/strategy changes require approval trail; approver, requester, diff, and evidence are stored; rollback is supported.

Title: Retention and evidence policy implementation
Acceptance Criteria: Retention is defined and enforced for orders, logs, decisions, and model artifacts; evidence pack can be exported for audit.

Title: User/admin accountability reports
Acceptance Criteria: Weekly or on-demand reports show overrides, rejected checks, break-glass events, kill-switch usage, and privileged actions by actor.

Title: Unified pre-trade policy engine
Acceptance Criteria: Every order passes through one policy layer; policies enforce instrument, strategy, time-window, venue, capital, and account constraints.

Title: Real-time risk limits engine
Acceptance Criteria: Per-strategy, symbol, account, and portfolio limits are enforced; drawdown, exposure, leverage, and concentration breaches block or reduce trading.

Title: Complete kill-switch and circuit-breaker lifecycle
Acceptance Criteria: Global/strategy/account/symbol kill switch exists; rearm requires approval; state is visible in API/UI/health; tests cover disable/rearm flows.

Title: Stale-quote and market-data safety controls
Acceptance Criteria: Orders are blocked on stale or degraded data; thresholds are configurable; degrade-to-no-new-orders mode is supported.

Title: Broker/exchange reject handling policy
Acceptance Criteria: Reject codes map to retry/no-retry/manual-action policies; duplicate orders are prevented across retries and reconnects.

Title: Intraday and end-of-day reconciliation hardening
Acceptance Criteria: Position/cash/order reconciliations run on schedule; mismatches are classified; critical mismatches freeze or throttle trading automatically.

Title: Formalize order state machine
Acceptance Criteria: Order states and transitions are explicit, documented, and enforced; invalid transitions are rejected; state-machine tests pass.

Title: End-to-end idempotent order submission
Acceptance Criteria: Retries, reconnects, and duplicate callbacks do not create duplicate live orders; idempotency keys are persisted and validated.

Title: Pluggable execution algorithms layer
Acceptance Criteria: Strategies can choose approved execution styles; execution selection is configurable and auditable; unsafe algorithms cannot bypass policy.

Title: Slippage and market-impact measurement
Acceptance Criteria: Arrival price, fill quality, shortfall, and slippage are captured per order; dashboards and alerts exist for degradation.

Title: Venue/broker failover logic
Acceptance Criteria: Degraded dependency path is defined; failover behavior is tested; trading falls back safely or pauses when failover conditions fail.

Title: Canonical market data layer
Acceptance Criteria: Tick, OHLCV, depth, timestamps, and derived features are normalized; quality flags are attached; data consumers use canonical interfaces.

Title: Market data quality validator
Acceptance Criteria: Missing ticks, timestamp drift, outliers, duplicate ticks, and crossed-book anomalies are detected; critical anomalies pause trading.

Title: Define market regime taxonomy
Acceptance Criteria: Regime classes are formally defined with business meaning and strategy implications; documentation is approved by quant and product.

Title: Regime detection engine v1 (deterministic baseline)
Acceptance Criteria: Interpretable baseline classifier exists; thresholds/features are versioned; backtest regime labels are stored and reproducible.

Title: Regime detection engine v2 (ML-based)
Acceptance Criteria: ML regime model beats baseline on agreed metrics; confidence score exposed; drift monitoring and rollback are live.

Title: Event-aware market context layer
Acceptance Criteria: Expiry, special sessions, major scheduled events, and auction windows are tagged; policies can adapt to event context.

Title: Standard strategy contract
Acceptance Criteria: Every strategy implements common interfaces for inputs, signals, sizing hooks, exits, risk hooks, and explainability output.

Title: Strategy versioning and deployment registry
Acceptance Criteria: Only approved versioned strategy artifacts can run in paper/shadow/live; rollback works; version lineage is queryable.

Title: Position sizing framework
Acceptance Criteria: Size decisions use capital, volatility, liquidity, confidence, and drawdown state; strategies cannot bypass sizing rules.

Title: Hierarchical decision engine
Acceptance Criteria: Signal generation, risk approval, execution choice, and portfolio constraints are separate layers; AI cannot directly bypass controls.

Title: Policy-bounded autonomy envelopes
Acceptance Criteria: Autonomous trading is permitted only within approved capital, turnover, time, symbol, and drawdown envelopes; breaches auto-disable.

Title: Strategy conflict resolver
Acceptance Criteria: Conflicting strategy actions are resolved by portfolio policy; no uncontrolled overtrading or duplicate intent on same instrument.

Title: Feature store and dataset lineage
Acceptance Criteria: Training and inference use governed feature definitions; lineage exists for every dataset and feature version; train/serve skew is measured.

Title: Model registry with approvals
Acceptance Criteria: Every model has owner, version, metrics, training window, status, and approval state; only approved models can reach shadow/live.

Title: Shadow inference in production
Acceptance Criteria: Models score live streams without affecting orders; shadow decisions are stored and compared against real outcomes.

Title: Drift, calibration, and degradation monitoring
Acceptance Criteria: Feature drift, label drift, calibration, and performance degradation are monitored; thresholds trigger alerting and auto-demotion.

Title: Explainability payloads for model decisions
Acceptance Criteria: Model outputs store top drivers, confidence, threshold crossings, and rejected alternatives; explainability is viewable in UI.

Title: Human-reviewed retraining workflow
Acceptance Criteria: Retrained models cannot auto-promote to live; approval requires validation evidence and signoff; rollback to prior model is supported.

Title: LLM usage boundaries and AI governance
Acceptance Criteria: LLMs are restricted to explanation, anomaly surfacing, and research assistance unless deterministic guardrails exist; no direct unrestricted order placement.

Title: High-fidelity backtest framework
Acceptance Criteria: Backtests include fees, slippage, latency, partial fills, rejects, and data gaps; results are reproducible and versioned.

Title: Historical market and decision replay
Acceptance Criteria: Any incident or trading day can be replayed deterministically with orders, risk checks, data events, and decisions.

Title: Paper trading environment parity
Acceptance Criteria: Paper trading uses the same code path as live except execution sink; environment separation is strict and visible.

Title: Shadow live mode
Acceptance Criteria: System generates hypothetical live actions alongside supervised trading; shadow-vs-live deltas are measurable and reviewable.

Title: Progressive rollout ladder
Acceptance Criteria: Deployment states disabled/paper/shadow/micro-live/capped-live/scaled-live are implemented with quantitative promotion criteria.

Title: Unified telemetry and tracing
Acceptance Criteria: Request/decision/order/broker events share correlation IDs; traces join UI action to live outcome; dashboards exist.

Title: Trading-specific alerting
Acceptance Criteria: Alerts fire for stale data, missing fills, reconcile mismatches, rejection spikes, latency spikes, abnormal turnover, and model drift.

Title: Trading SLOs and error budgets
Acceptance Criteria: SLOs exist for data freshness, decision latency, order ack, reconciliation freshness, and alert response; error budgets are reviewed.

Title: Graceful degradation modes
Acceptance Criteria: Platform can degrade to read-only, close-only, no-new-orders, or supervised-only; dependency failure behavior is deterministic and tested.

Title: Incident tooling and postmortem workflow
Acceptance Criteria: One-click incident snapshot exists; postmortem template and action tracking are standardized; incidents can be reconstructed.

Title: Replace free-text tenant switching
Acceptance Criteria: Tenant selection is entitlement-aware and not manual text entry; switching unauthorized tenants is impossible from UI.

Title: Redesign Control Tower
Acceptance Criteria: Screen shows strategy state, current regime, risk consumption, active policies, blocked actions, health, and kill-switch status clearly.

Title: Decision explainability UI
Acceptance Criteria: User can inspect why a trade was or was not taken; signal, regime, risk, policy, and execution rationale are visible.

Title: Incident and override console
Acceptance Criteria: Manual overrides are explicit, bounded, reversible where allowed, and fully audited; current override state is visible.

Title: Accessibility remediation
Acceptance Criteria: Labels, focus states, dialogs, keyboard navigation, reduced motion, contrast, and status semantics meet internal accessibility standard.

Title: Restore and ship full automated test suite
Acceptance Criteria: Unit, integration, contract, and E2E tests are present in repo and run in CI; release candidates include test artifacts.

Title: Critical-path integration tests
Acceptance Criteria: Tests cover auth, authz, tenant isolation, order submission, rejects, reconciliation, kill switch, and session expiry.

Title: Property-based and fuzz testing for state machines
Acceptance Criteria: Invalid state transitions, timing races, duplicate callbacks, and malformed inputs are automatically explored and safely handled.

Title: Performance, load, and soak testing
Acceptance Criteria: Tests cover market-open bursts, reconnect storms, long-running sessions, and large portfolio volumes; thresholds are documented.

Title: Chaos and dependency-failure testing
Acceptance Criteria: Broker outage, stale feed, DB failover, delayed fills, message duplication, and clock skew scenarios are executed and pass defined outcomes.

Title: Model validation pack
Acceptance Criteria: Walk-forward, regime-wise, drawdown, stability, stress-window, and ablation tests exist for every promoted model.

Title: CI/CD gated promotion pipeline
Acceptance Criteria: Build, lint, test, scan, sign, and deploy gates exist; critical failures block promotion automatically.

Title: Dependency and container hardening
Acceptance Criteria: SBOM, vulnerability scans, base-image policy, patch SLAs, and .dockerignore are in place and enforced.

Title: Strict environment separation
Acceptance Criteria: Dev/test/paper/shadow/live environments are isolated by credentials, configs, data, and network path; accidental crossover tests fail.

Title: Safe rollback for code and config
Acceptance Criteria: Code rollback and config/strategy rollback are one-step, documented, tested, and auditable.

Title: Release policy and approval windows
Acceptance Criteria: Trading-hours release rules, freeze windows, and approval requirements are documented and enforced operationally.

Title: Data inventory and classification
Acceptance Criteria: Personal data, sensitive operational data, secrets, logs, and model artifacts are classified and owned.

Title: Data minimization and masking
Acceptance Criteria: Logs, UI, and exports mask sensitive fields; only necessary personal data is stored and exposed by role.

Title: Retention and deletion workflows
Acceptance Criteria: Retention schedules are enforced; deletion/export workflows exist where applicable; exceptions are documented.

Title: Notice, access transparency, and privacy controls
Acceptance Criteria: User/admin data processing notices exist; access to personal data is logged; privacy controls are documented and tested.

Title: Portfolio construction layer
Acceptance Criteria: Multiple strategies compete for capital through portfolio rules; portfolio-level constraints override local strategy intent when needed.

Title: Dynamic capital allocator
Acceptance Criteria: Allocation responds to regime, confidence, drawdown, and correlation within policy bounds; changes are auditable and bounded.

Title: Regime-to-strategy routing
Acceptance Criteria: Strategy activation/deactivation is driven by approved regime routing rules; routing version is recorded for every decision.

Title: Self-evaluation and auto-throttling
Acceptance Criteria: If live behavior deviates from expected envelope, strategy is throttled, demoted, or disabled automatically; alerts are raised.

Title: Continuous learning sandbox
Acceptance Criteria: Online or continuous learning is allowed only in sandbox; no direct self-modification of live trading behavior occurs.
